source_question: Which part of the arithmetic inverse theorem is already supplied by classical positive-measure Laplace uniqueness?

primary_source.title: Bernstein Functions: Theory and Applications
primary_source.authenticated_metadata: Title, authors, publisher, copyright year and print ISBN checked in the preview front matter.
primary_source.extraction_status: Primary publisher-distributed preview read, including full Proposition 1.2 and Theorem 1.4 proofs. No local source retained.

extracted_results.locator: Proposition 1.2, printed page 2, PDF page 14 under one-based indexing
extracted_results.paraphrase: A measure supported on the nonnegative half-line is uniquely determined by its Laplace transform; finiteness is equivalent to finite transform limit at zero.
extracted_results.notation_translation: The source measure becomes sum_j w_j delta_lambda_j; the transform variable is real depth s>0.
extracted_results.hypotheses: The present weights are positive with finite total mass, and all frequencies are positive and bounded.
extracted_results.application: Valid as an alternative general uniqueness proof. Our elementary ordered peeling proof does not depend on this leaf.

extracted_results.locator: Theorem 1.4, printed page 3, PDF page 15 under one-based indexing
extracted_results.paraphrase: A completely monotone function is the Laplace transform of a unique positive measure on the nonnegative half-line, and conversely a finite such transform is completely monotone.
extracted_results.application: Valid classical comparison for the positive depth restriction. It does not supply beta, a, excluded-prime reconstruction, or bounded-window arithmetic instability.
